items.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Oh, I know who he's talking about. Is it Mahaney? ... [INTERVIEWEE] I don't remember that song...

ctx.x: Oh, that's late years, huh? Yeah. I thought it wasn't what I'm talking about. It wasn't Ramping Ma Rainey, but it put him in the mind.

Oh, I know who he's talking about. Is it Mahaney? No, it's a white woman, huh? What's that? Is that a white woman that tries to sing like Ma Rainey in them? No, she was calling. Oh, I don't know who it would be then. Why are there so many of them?

I don't remember that song about if you're broken hearted and your man is out of town, go to the river and jump right up. Take your chance. Take your chance. Take your chance. Make Mennowiller. If he don't come back, let me tell you what to do. Jump right up with boys, cause you ain't no more than you. Cause I thought my man would kiss him morning, noon, and night.
